title: Qt: Move Recent Capture files to model implementation
description:
Moving the recent capture files to a model impelementation as well
as implementing a WorkspaceState class for future reduction of
reliance on recent.?

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)

notes.body:
For now this seems to be overhead code. But it removes a bit of code that ran duplicated on both Qt apps and also adds the model. I've also cleaned up the welcome page in general a bit, so that it is now properly designed according to Qt/QML guidelines (using layout boxes as they should). This is in preparation for bit of redesign on the WelcomePage

@mmann78 this is the patch I referred to yesterday. The one where I "try" to start moving our stuff to be a bit more Qt compliant. The WorkspaceState being the first of those classes. Note, that there is no built-in separation that might be useful if we want to have different Workspaces for different files. There are settings in the UI that are document agnostic and some aren't. For instance, it is not that unthinkable that the geometry settings are not document agnostic if we were ever to go to a multi-document system. But even if we would do that, we could just move the WorkspaceState::instance() into a WSDocument superclass (as a member) and it would require very little adaption to have it document agnostic again. For now, I think this is the correct first step on removing recent.c/h as a first test-ballon on how to clean up the ui/.... c-mess.

Yes, this definitely has some conflicts with the direction I was trying to go. So, I'll try to explain what I was doing and how I was trying to get there, because some of my code may still be salvageable (it's okay if it's not).  I also want to make sure I understand the direction you're trying to go, to help out in getting there.

The ui/ folder has a poor re-implementation of the preference file functionality, so I was trying to extend and refactor the "epan preferences", so that we could have "UI preferences" in the same way where Wireshark would register modules and submodules just like dissectors (and parts of epan) do (yea common code!).  I was just trying to standardize the read/write/storage of the preferences (and have the data to present to the UI layer, NOT write it directly like recent_read_dynamic/read_set_recent_pair_dynamic does).  That was the "layer separation" I was after (and thought it was language (C/C++) agnostic).

However, it looks like you replaced the "read recent_common" file functionality with a single line:
`bool success = parseRecentFile(filePath, [&newFileList](const QString &key, const QString &value)`
Is your intention to expand on the "keys" covered here to handle _all_ "preferences" in the recent_common file and that `WorkspaceState::loadCommonState` will be the sole source of reading recent_common (and there is no need for the "reading preference file" common code)?  And then presumably follow it up with a function that writes recent_common (because that is clearly missing from your code ATM)?  Does Qt have a "more native" way of storing window position (and some of the other "GUI preferences) or are we still going to continue to use recent and recent_common files through WorkspaceState (and just have C++ handling it instead of C)?  If that's the case, then I don't need to be expanding our current preference support to handle the UI layer.

Related to the "preference-like" functionality was that some "UI preferences" could be overridden with the -o commandline option.  This was also something I thought I could leverage with the common code of the preference API. I don't currently see any hooks you've added for -o preferences.  Which brings me to the question of "Do you think the data in recent and recent_common" is sliced up correctly?  Will WorkspaceState (eventually) cover it all for "backwards compatibility", even though some of the "preferences" will want to be overridden by the commandline?

So for the part of WorkspaceState. Yes, that should become a total replacement of the current recent / recent_common functionality in recent.c/h. We already are using the geometry hex string provided by Qt for saving the GUI geometry but we store information redundantly (aka we also store x,y,width,height separately, although all of those are already stored in the geometry string). We do not currently use "saveState" which would allow us for instance to save the header column width, which we currently store manually, or if columns are hidden or not (which we store currently in epan). The column representation logic being in epan has for a very very long time been a pain for me, but for now I would keep it there. Columns itself are fine in epan, but display options like hidden state or geometry should be moved out of there.

As of reading the recent files, YES there is a much easier way to do it. We can describe Models that have basically the technical definition for each field and have it read through QSettings. We would get variants, but we could convert them type-safe into QObjects. That would also allow us to much easier switch to a different data-format in the future, like JSON for instance. That is where I am going with this. Also, we could then utilise the Q_PROPERTY system allowing us to iterate over the configuration for converting for instance or for versioning it, so we could upgrade/downgrade the settings for different versions. Not talking about the general preferences here, but gui stuff should be more flexible to what we actually need.

As for the command line handling, I am aware of the flag. I dont like the commandline handling also, but one at a time. For that for instance we could just use QCommandLineParser. Does the same stuff than commandline.c and would already be part of Qt. At the same time would help make organising the options a bit easier, as well as translation! We could actually have the texts properly translated for the options, and the formatting would be handled by Qt internally. The big issue there is the assignment of the parsed values. They all apply at different stages during boot up. But if we put that in a proper utility class, it would be really easy to substitute the commandline structure as well. At least in theory. What makes the commandline handling so hard is its tight integration with the capture options. It would clean-up the startup of the application significantly though and would reduce one more thing that we can't translate as of right now.

You've certainly given me enough stuff to google, but what "file format" do you see QSettings taking? I thought we wanted some of these "preferences" to be shareable (I think more of enabling/disabling features than individual window positions), so they still need to fit into the profile architecture.  Should we have QSettings functionality to recreate recent/recent_common "as is" (maybe removing the window position members that may be from the GTK days) for backwards compatibily or are you thinking 5.0 files may not be backwards compatible with 4.x?
With "file format" I meant, we are currently using INI-file format. But if we use a class like QSettings, switching to - let's say - Json, it would be practically be a one-liner

I agree it would be easy to do, the question is should we do it for 5.0 or stay with the INI format for backwards compatibility (I may try my hand at adding support for "saveState" and writing the recent file.)
We should definitely stay, I am just saying it gives us options. Right now, we are boxed in. But I guess this is a discussion for another time and thread
On the subject of JSON, I wonder if it would be useful to add a JSON key/value store in addition to or as a replacement for UATs.

Slightly different question based on the CI/CD failure - I know we've talked about removing Qt5 support for 5.0.  When can a commit from master that fails Qt5 compilation be acceptable? Do we just deprecate (remove) the Ubuntu Qt5 builder?

I personally think we would want to enforce Qt6 in CMake before accepting a commit that fails Qt5 compilation, but removing the Qt5 builder (or setting it to "allowed to fail" in the CI/CD) settings would allow it.

I started down the road of removing Qt5 support (more so than enforcing Qt6) but was reminded of the Qt5 builder and I wasn't sure how definite we were on 5.0 not supporting Qt5 (because I'm with you in that we should do it earlier in the dev cycle)

Ok, that it fails Qt5 was on accident. I simply did not care for compatibility while writing this code and I would be ok if we start enforcing Qt5 deprecation as of right now. That would make this code purely 5.0 of course. But I also think recreating compatibility should not be too hard. I'll try to see if I can do it with the patch and we can still decide which directions we want to go.
I know @oakimk had some issues with having to support RHEL8 which doesn't come with Qt5, but I think it's better to make the change earlier in the dev cycle.
isn't this failure just due to fancy c++14 functionality, which we have **NOT** lift to yet
Hm, you mean the second argument for the lambda? I can try to test this out, yes
I think we probably could require C++14 at this point. Qt6 will require C++17, but I think any platform we support now supports C++14
not RHEL8 ...

I just stumbled across something. We still only require C++11 according to our CMakeLists.txt. BUT, I am building Stratoshark (as makes sense since I am doing GUI stuff that affects both), and when you build Stratoshark, falcodump OR dumpcalls it forces C++17 (!) @geraldcombs not sure, if you should not document this a bit better. Because this basically means, that we loose a TON of compatibility build system wise and I am not certain, people are aware. Makes NO difference when developing stuff, but when submitting MRs it makes a huge difference on what to check beforehand and what not. Personally, I was NOT aware of that.

Btw, we are also forcing C++17 WHENEVER we are building Wireshark using Qt6, although Qt6 itself does NOT force it. That looks also like something we should have documented a bit better, although it is in there for a while now
RHEL 8 uses GCC 8 by default, which is C++14 (but not 17), AIUI: https://gcc.gnu.org/projects/cxx-status.html#cxx14
aha, then it's just that with Qt5 we build with forced -std=c++11
Correct.
yes we do, but I fixed the issues nethertheless
yep, builds fine now

Qt6 does require C++17, see here:

https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/cmake-get-started.html#:~:text=Qt%206%20requires%20a%20compiler,Qt%20available%20in%20CMake%20projects.

Falcodump, dumpcalls, and the falco-events plugin require C++ 17 because that's what [libsinsp requires](https://github.com/falcosecurity/libs/blob/master/cmake/modules/CompilerFlags.cmake#L25). I'll see if I can set that for each target instead of globally.

With the left and right side margin now MinimumExpanding, this significantly increases the minimum horizontal resolution of Wireshark at all times (including when the Welcome page is not visible.)

English: 725px -> 958px
Russian: 859px -> 1092px
Japanese: 878px -> 1111px

This thus reopens #19861.

Good to put that on my radar for the other change. Fixing the numbers in the layout is still the wrong approach. When we have a language issue due to language wrapping wrongly, the right fix would have been to make the box size aware for the text and adapt the stretchers whenever the language is applied. NOT fixing the value in the design. With Qt UI you should avoid fixing down on the design as much as possible when it comes to constraints. So sizes, colours, styles, ... and let them be handled by the classes. Otherwise you have different parts of the application fight each other to get the stuff across.

Removing the stretch factor and having the left and right stretch the same as the middle means that there are large empty alleys on the left and right side at large resolutions, even when the names of the links at the bottom still have to word wrap in languages like Russian and Japanese.
I get that. But this is an intermediary change towards something new (as I put it on Discord).

Another minor issue - when "Export Specified Packets" is used, the newly created file is intentionally not opened but is set to the top entry in the recent capture files list. However, after this change, the newly created file is disabled in the recent captures list (from the File menu) so it's impossible to quickly switch to the newly created file via the recent capture files list.

I think this is because the recent menu is updated before the queued check for the file status completes, and (since the recent QMenu is not a model view) it doesn't get updated when it completes. Something like:

```c++
connect(WorkspaceState::instance(), &WorkspaceState::recentFileStatusChanged, this, &MainWindow::populateRecentCapturesMenu);
```

in the MainWindow constructor would work, I think.

+/**
+ * @brief Qt model for displaying recent capture files.
+ *
+ * This is a thin wrapper over WorkspaceState - it doesn't store data,
+ * just provides a Qt model interface for views.
+ *
+ * Thread safety: Assumes single-threaded access (UI thread only).
+ */
+class RecentCaptureFilesListModel : public QAbstractListModel
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+public:
+    /**
+     * @brief Custom data roles for RecentCaptureFilesListModel.
+     */
+    enum RecentFileRoles {
+        FilenameRole = Qt::UserRole,
+        FileSizeRole,
+        AccessibleRole
+    };
+
+    explicit RecentCaptureFilesListModel(QObject *parent = nullptr);
+    ~RecentCaptureFilesListModel();
+
+    int rowCount(const QModelIndex &parent = QModelIndex()) const override;
+    QVariant data(const QModelIndex &index, int role = Qt::DisplayRole) const override;
+    Qt::ItemFlags flags(const QModelIndex &index) const override;
+
+private slots:
+    void invalidateModel();
+};
+
+/**
+ * @brief Proxy model that reverses row order for display (newest first).
+ *
+ * WorkspaceState stores files oldest-first (matching the file format).
+ * This proxy reverses the order so the UI shows newest files at top.
+ */
+class RecentCaptureFilesReverseProxyModel : public QSortFilterProxyModel
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+public:
+    explicit RecentCaptureFilesReverseProxyModel(QObject *parent = nullptr);
+
+    QModelIndex mapToSource(const QModelIndex &proxyIndex) const override;
+    QModelIndex mapFromSource(const QModelIndex &sourceIndex) const override;
+};
+
+/**
+ * @brief Item delegate that formats recent file entries with size info.
+ *
+ * Displays: "filename (10 MB)" or "filename (not found)" for inaccessible files.
+ * Inaccessible files are rendered in italic.
+ */
+class RecentCaptureFilesDelegate : public QStyledItemDelegate
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+public:
+    explicit RecentCaptureFilesDelegate(QObject *parent = nullptr);
+
+    QString displayText(const QVariant &value, const QLocale &locale) const override;
+    void initStyleOption(QStyleOptionViewItem *option, const QModelIndex &index) const override;
+
+private:

+};

+/** @file
+ *
+ * Workspace state management - handles persistent UI state between sessions
+ *
+ * This provides Qt-native access to the state files managed by ui/recent.c.
+ * Currently runs parallel to the existing C code for gradual migration.
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef WORKSPACE_STATE_H
+#define WORKSPACE_STATE_H
+
+#include "config.h"
+
+#include <QObject>
+#include <QStringList>
+#include <QFileInfo>
+#include <QList>
+#include <functional>
+
+/**
+ * @brief Information about a recent capture file.
+ *
+ * Stores the filename along with cached status information
+ * (size and accessibility) that is updated asynchronously.
+ */
+struct RecentFileInfo {
+    QString filename;
+    qint64 size = 0;
+    bool accessible = false;
+};
+
+/**
+ * @brief Manages workspace state that persists between sessions.
+ *
+ * This class provides Qt-native access to the "recent" settings.
+ * It currently runs parallel to ui/recent.c for gradual migration.
+ *
+ * Usage:
+ *   WorkspaceState::instance()->loadCommonState();
+ *   QStringList files = WorkspaceState::instance()->recentCaptureFiles();
+ *
+ * The singleton pattern avoids adding more dependencies to MainApplication.
+ */
+class WorkspaceState : public QObject
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+
+public:
+    /**
+     * @brief Returns the singleton instance.
+     *
+     * Thread-safe in C++11 and later (Meyer's Singleton).
+     */
+    static WorkspaceState* instance();
+
+    virtual ~WorkspaceState();
+
+    // Prevent copying
+    WorkspaceState(const WorkspaceState&) = delete;
+    WorkspaceState& operator=(const WorkspaceState&) = delete;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Load state from the recent_common file.
+     *
+     * Call this during application startup after recent_read_static() has been called.
+     *
+     * @param[out] errorPath If loading fails, contains the path that failed.
+     * @param[out] errorCode If loading fails, contains the errno.
+     * @return true on success, false on failure.
+     */
+    bool loadCommonState(QString *errorPath = nullptr, int *errorCode = nullptr);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Get the path to the recent_common file.
+     *
+     * @return Full path to the recent_common file.
+     */
+    QString recentCommonFilePath() const;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Get the path to the profile-specific recent file.
+     *
+     * @return Full path to the recent file for the current profile.
+     */
+    QString recentProfileFilePath() const;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Get the list of recently opened capture files.
+     *
+     * @return List of file info structs, most recent last.
+     */
+    const QList<RecentFileInfo>& recentCaptureFiles() const;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Get just the filenames of recent capture files.
+     *
+     * Convenience method for code that only needs the paths.
+     *
+     * @return List of file paths, most recent last.
+     */
+    QStringList recentCaptureFilenames() const;
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Add a capture file to the recent files list.
+     *
+     * @param filePath The path to the capture file.
+     */
+    void addRecentCaptureFile(const QString &filePath);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Remove a capture file from the recent files list.
+     *
+     * @param filePath The path to remove.
+     */
+    void removeRecentCaptureFile(const QString &filePath);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Clear all recent capture files.
+     */
+    void clearRecentCaptureFiles();
+
+signals:
+    /**
+     * @brief Emitted when the recent capture files list changes.
+     */
+    void recentCaptureFilesChanged();
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Emitted when a file's status (size/accessibility) is updated.
+     *
+     * @param filename The file whose status was updated.
+     */
+    void recentFileStatusChanged(const QString &filename);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Emitted when state is loaded from disk.
+     */
+    void stateLoaded();
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Emitted when state is saved to disk.
+     */
+    void stateSaved();
+
+protected:
+    explicit WorkspaceState(QObject *parent = nullptr);
+
+private slots:
+    /**
+     * @brief Slot called when async file status check completes.
+     */
+    void onFileStatusChecked(const QString &filename, qint64 size, bool accessible);
+
+private:
+    /**
+     * @brief Parse a recent file and extract key-value pairs.
+     *
+     * @param filePath Path to the recent file.
+     * @param handler Callback for each key-value pair found.
+     * @return true on success, false on failure.
+     */
+    bool parseRecentFile(const QString &filePath,
+                         std::function<void(const QString &key, const QString &value)> handler);
+
+    /**
+     * @brief Queue an async file status check for a file.
+     */
+    void queueFileStatusCheck(const QString &filename);
+
+    QList<RecentFileInfo> recent_capture_files_;
+
+    static constexpr const char* RECENT_COMMON_FILE_NAME = "recent_common";
+    static constexpr const char* RECENT_PROFILE_FILE_NAME = "recent";
+    static constexpr const char* KEY_CAPTURE_FILE = "recent.capture_file";
+};
+
+#endif // WORKSPACE_STATE_H

commits_data.message:
Qt: Move Recent Capture files to model implementation

Moving the recent capture files to a model impelementation as well
as implementing a WorkspaceState class for future reduction of
reliance on recent.?

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)
